rationale: Needs both Talarico (TX) and El-Sayed (MI) to win. Late-October TX polls show Talarico up 2-4 (Marist, Emerson, UH, TPOR), but Texas polls have historically overstated Democrats, so ~45%. El-Sayed leads Rogers by ~2-3 in averages (Cook Toss-Up), ~65%. Outcomes are positively correlated through the national environment, so the joint is ~0.35.

Minnesota has not elected a Republican senator since 2002 (base rate strongly D). Flanagan leads Tafoya by 3-5 in averages (RCP +3.4, SurveyUSA +3, Rasmussen/Trafalgar +3), although Cook moved it to Lean D over the fraud scandal. In a favorable D midterm, a consistent lead in a blue state gives ~0.82.

The deposit rate is 2.50% after a September hike. Consensus and OIS pricing (about 3% hike probability as of Oct 26) point to a hold on Oct 29, with no new staff projections at this meeting. A search result showed a prediction-market figure, which I discarded. Some inflation risk remains, so ~0.04.

A fragile post-June ceasefire is in place. Trump blocked an Israeli operation in October and pledged no US strikes before the Nov 3 midterms, but the NYT reports that US and Israeli militaries have specific plans for renewed strikes after the midterms. Israel's own election (Oct 27) is a constraint that also ends soon. The Nov 4-15 window is exposed but short, and plans often slip, so ~0.45.

SC is strongly R (base rate: no Democratic senator since 2005). The race is unusually close: the R nominee (reportedly Graham's appointed successor, Darline Graham Nordone) leads Andrews by ~2 in averages, and the latest D-internal poll has Andrews +1. Andrews has a huge money advantage. Partisan lean plus the small R polling lead gives ~0.72.

Acton leads Ramaswamy in most quality polls (Marist +7, BGSU/YouGov +6, Fox +2; averages +2.6 to +4.4), and Sabato moved the race to Lean D. However, Ohio polls have overstated Democrats in recent cycles and the state leans R. A search result quoted prediction-market odds, which I discarded. ~0.60.

Republicans need to hold enough seats that Democrats fall short of a net +4. Non-market models give Democrats 56% (DDHQ), 60% (VoteHub) and ~75% (Silver Bulletin), with Pollsmax at 45%. Democrats lead narrowly in TX, AK, OH, MI and MN, but the race is polling-error sensitive. Market figures appeared in a result and were discarded. R control ~0.36.

Only a local Oleshky humanitarian truce has been agreed (location-specific, so it does not qualify). The next technical talks are set for mid-November, and the Kremlin says it will not ease the offensive. A general ceasefire agreement within 5 days is very unlikely.

Incumbent senators usually win, and Alaska leans R, but Peltola leads narrowly in most October polls (averages Peltola +1 to +2.4, final-round RCV 51-49) and Sabato rates it Lean D. Alaska polls have sometimes underestimated Republicans, which partly offsets this. A result quoted prediction-market odds, which I discarded. ~0.42.

anthropic.com/news shows Fable 5.1 released Sep 15, 2026, plus the 5.5 versions of Opus, Sonnet and Haiku (Sep 22 to Oct 7), but no Fable 5.5 announcement as of Oct 26. Releasing it within 5 days, only ~6 weeks after Fable 5.1, is unlikely but not impossible given the 5.5 rollout cadence.

Resolves YES if no US-Iran Hormuz agreement is announced by Nov 2. Talks are indirect and stalled: Iran says the US is 'not serious', the IRGC denied a reopening offer, and Trump raised strikes. The US-Iran MOU lapsed in August. With 7 days left and no agreement imminent, ~0.94.

The Houthis are still attacking Saudi targets, including Riyadh airport and pipelines. Saudi-Iran talks in Tehran produced no communique, and Riyadh officially rejects a new ceasefire. A reported $1B deal is unconfirmed and the Houthis were not party to it. Both sides would need to announce a ceasefire within 5 days, so ~0.07.
